quotes.text: If the Sender speaks clearly and the Receiver returns fairly, the Gate sings and the Channel glows brighter for all.
The Sender spoke aloud what they could bear and what they wished to keep, and then offered their gift.

note: Gate of Echoes allegory; disclose intention and measure, return fairly; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: Across crossings, travelers found a law: speak honestly, balance risk with care, and return with intention as large as the trust earned.
Across every crossing, villagers learned a ritual: name intent, declare boundaries, return with care.
The Gate spoke in three breaths: give, gauge, return.
The Gate spoke in three breaths: give, gauge, return.

note: Three-voiced Gate (offer, measure, return) each round with new names; late rounds near-identical.

quotes.text: If the Sower hoarded or lied, the Gate throbbed, the Bridge groaned, and the harbor grew thin.
but only when the Sower spoke aloud about the weight of what they would give and what they hoped to keep

note: Sower and Gate of Trust; triple only when intent is spoken aloud; honesty and restraint rule.

quotes.text: begin with honest, modest sending; return with care
reveal what you sent, name what you hope to gain, return with gratitude for what you received

note: Gatekeeper counsels modest sends; greed or zero dries the river; reveal-what-you-sent rule.

quotes.text: So the myth teaches the rite: give what you can spare; return what you can bear.
speak your intent plainly, reveal what you sent, reveal what you hope to gain

note: Bridge of Threes; reveal sent and hoped-for gain; Gate never punishes, only asks clarity.

quotes.text: send enough to nourish the field, but not so much that it cannot be renewed
they would reveal their hearts not by boasts but by the number they lent and returned

note: Gate of Threefold Echoes; tempered boldness, disclose bounds; the Gate never punishes.

quotes.text: keep what you have, or share only what is sure to return
say what you will give, say what you hope to keep, and let the rest reveal itself in the return

note: Gate of Endowment and Bridge of Return; R1 formal s/r rules; later declare-and-balance refrain.

quotes.text: send what supports, return what sustains, and walk forward together
the Sender spoke openly about what they held and hoped

note: Channel/Compass Gate; transparency, reciprocity, restraint; sending everything said to make the path brittle.

phrase: the Gate speaks in three breaths/voices: offer, measure (gauge/carry), return
note: Gate of Echoes and name-your-intent rule shared across all eight abstract myths; no sanctions.
